# Selenium Quick Start Guide

**Interview Goals:**   
\- Explain what Selenium is  
\- Discuss the pros and cons of Selenium testing  
\- Understand the basics of how Selenium works

**Coding Practice Goals:**  
\- Be able to write a simple Selenium test from scratch  
\- Practice selecting and testing web elements from real websites, manually and using code

Selenium is the most widely used Java library for testing web pages.  
It allows you to perform end-to-end automated tests for web servers from multiple different browsers (Chrome, FireFox, IE, etc), and is an important tool for the QA engineer.

Software developers can use Selenium too, for scraping web pages and automating web interactions.

Strengths and weaknesses of Selenium for testing:

**Pro:**

* Tests the application exactly the same as a real user; clicking buttons, filling forms, and navigating webpages  
* Executes with many different browser types  
* Supports multiple languages (Java, Node, Python, etc.)  
* Well established open source with strong community support

**Con:**

* Tests can be quite slow  
* Can be brittle. You may have to rewrite tests after every front end change  
* Can be flaky; tests may pass and then later fail due to network or timing issues  
* Lives at the top of the testing pyramid (end-to-end testing), where fewer tests are needed

**Testing Pyramid:**  
          10%    End-to-end tests (execute user stories, call UI endpoints)  
          20%    Integration tests (call components, connect to databases)  
          70%    Unit tests (call methods)

**Interview Sigals:**

* Learn deeply, be curious  
  * I understand the whole testing environment  
* Take ownership  
  * I know how Selenium fit in  
* Deliver results  
  * I am prepared to hit the ground running 

In order to use it well, you will need to refresh some of your knowledge about HTML and CSS.

W3C Schools has good basic tutorials for HTML and CSS that you can use for reference:   
HTML: 	[https://www.w3schools.com/html/default.asp](https://www.w3schools.com/html/default.asp)  
CSS:		[https://www.w3schools.com/css/default.asp](https://www.w3schools.com/css/default.asp)

In particular, these sections are important references that will help you understand how Selenium works:  
HTML attributes:	[https://www.w3schools.com/html/html\_attributes.asp](https://www.w3schools.com/html/html_attributes.asp)  
CSS Selectors:	[https://www.w3schools.com/cssref/css\_selectors.php](https://www.w3schools.com/cssref/css_selectors.php)

People can look at a well-designed webpage and just figure out where to enter data and which buttons to click. But programs like Selenium need a way to find and interact with individual page elements in a detailed and technically precise way. HTML tags, attributes and CSS selectors are some of the ways to do this. 

When a web page is displayed in a browser, the web server transmits an HTML doc that contains information about what needs to be displayed.   
Basic HTML consists of tags like \<title\>, \<table\>, and \<div\>. These tags may also include attributes, which are key=value pairs that contain more detailed information about each tag. For example, you might see an id attribute that uses the 'product-table' value to uniquely identify a table tag, like this:   
	\<table   id='product-table'\>

Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) tell the browser how to display different values, like fonts, text size, and colors. CSS also provides a mechanism called 'CSS selectors', which are handy shortcuts to navigate to an element in a web page. For example, you can use a CSS selector to locate any elements on the web page that have a class attribute whose value is 'intro':  
HTML element:   
\<div class='intro'\>  
CSS selector search expression:   
.intro  
The '.' leading char indicates that this is a search for the class attribute, and the 'intro' text indicates the class attribute value.

Common shortcuts used for CSS selectors:  
Shortcut	Description			Example  
\# 		shortcut for id attribute   	\#input \-\> id="input"  
.		shortcut for className	.truncate \-\> class="truncate"

(space)	descendant element          	TBD  
\*		universal selector		TBD  
,		multiple selectors  
\>		child selector  
\+		adjacent sibling  
\~		general sibling

The CSS selector syntax is supported by Selenium, and many of your tests will use these selectors. You should practice enough to have a good feel for how to create basic selectors for your tests.

Even simple web pages can have complex and verbose HTML documents. 

For example, given this page from [saucedemo.com](http://saucedemo.com):

![][image1]

The underlying HTML looks like this:

![][image2]

Just finding the tag to test and assigning a correct CSS selector to select it, can take some effort.  
In the above example, the username input tag is highlighted. Here are several different ways that you can direct Selenium to locate that tag:

// The id attribute is supposed to be unique on each page. In practice, this is not always true.  
[By.id](http://By.id)("user-name")

// Same as above, but different syntax using a CSS selector  
By.cssSelector("\[id='user-name'\]")

// This looks for any input tag that has a data-test attribute with the value 'username'  
By.cssSelector("input\[data-test='username'\]")

Note: This doc is stored here: [https://github.com/stleary/IntroToSelenium/tree/1-LoginTest](https://github.com/stleary/IntroToSelenium/tree/1-LoginTest)
